title: Be an Indistractable Lover
coreMove: Use structure to protect presence with the person you love, then let the structure disappear into actual attention.
sourcePressure: The closing chapter synthesizes internal triggers, external triggers, traction, and pacts into relational attention and defended presence.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would turn intimacy into productivity or imply systems can replace tenderness.

hook: Be an Indistractable Lover as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: partners reconnecting after one returns from wildfire duty
exampleSpecs.audience: partner who wants presence after days of crisis alerts
exampleSpecs.stakes: the first hour home can become another emergency briefing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: they place the duty pager in a hallway bowl and start with one question about what the other carried today
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A duty pager rests in a blue hallway bowl.

exampleSpecs.domain: couple managing infertility paperwork and grief
exampleSpecs.audience: partners whose phones become escape hatches during hard talks
exampleSpecs.stakes: the relationship needs room for pain without one person disappearing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: they name the grief, set the clinic folder aside, and agree that one hand on the table means stay present
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A clinic folder is closed beside a linen table runner.

exampleSpecs.domain: long-married partners running a small marina together
exampleSpecs.audience: spouses who only talk through tasks and weather
exampleSpecs.stakes: work logistics have crowded out affection
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, dinner turns into dock assignments; after, they put the tide notebook away for the first twenty minutes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A tide notebook is shut beside two chipped enamel plates.

exampleSpecs.domain: new parents handing off a premature infant's care
exampleSpecs.audience: couple whose attention is consumed by monitors
exampleSpecs.stakes: care structure must support tenderness, not erase it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: they choose one monitor-check rhythm, then sit shoulder to shoulder without narrating every beep
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A neonatal monitor printout lies beside a soft cotton blanket.

exampleSpecs.domain: partners separated by seasonal fishing work
exampleSpecs.audience: couple whose calls collapse into distracted multitasking
exampleSpecs.stakes: distance needs defended attention or resentment grows quietly
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: they review the last scattered call and choose a dockside call time with gear stowed away
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A coil of dock line sits beside a scheduled call card.

exampleSpecs.domain: retired spouses learning a new language together
exampleSpecs.audience: partners tempted to turn shared practice into correction
exampleSpecs.stakes: attention should protect connection, not winning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one spouse closes the grammar app after the planned drill and asks the other to tell a memory using three new words
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A bilingual phrase card rests beside a closed grammar app.

skillTargets: identify when a scenario calls for: Use structure to protect presence with the person you love, then let the structure disappear into actual attention.

explain why the tempting weak version fails: A weak run would turn intimacy into productivity or imply systems can replace tenderness.
use chapter-specific terms such as relationships, presence, traction, internal triggers in transfer scenarios

tryThisNowSpec: Before the next conversation with someone you love, remove one cue, name one intention, and begin with one undivided question.
